answer: Copying the same citations across 233 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 233 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the juniper index resolves every citation against the island checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the velvet audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 2029 identities would post 3244 proofs and burn roughly 27 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
